perf.summary: Accumulate into a local long and branchlessly saturate, instead of read-modify-write on pathCount[u] each edge.
perf.currentCost: Each edge does a load of pathCount[u], an overflow-guard compare/branch, and a store back to pathCount[u]. The store-to-load dependency on the same memory location each iteration serializes the inner loop and adds a hard-to-predict branch per edge.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist accumulation: 'long acc = pathCount[u]; for (e...) { long add = pathCount[v]; long sum = unchecked(acc + add); acc = (acc > long.MaxValue - add) ? long.MaxValue : sum; } pathCount[u] = acc;'. Better, since pathCount values are non-negative, detect saturation branchlessly via 'sum < 0' (sign-bit of overflow for non-negative operands) using a select: 'acc = sum < 0 ? long.MaxValue : sum;'.
perf.rationale: Keeping the running sum in a register removes the per-edge memory store and its store-forwarding dependency, and 'sum < 0' is a correct overflow test when both operands are non-negative (two non-negative longs overflow exactly when their wrapped sum becomes negative), turning the guard into a branchless cmov. Shorter dependency chain and one store at the end instead of per edge.
perf.risk: Requires that pathCount[v] and the running acc stay non-negative and never reach exactly long.MaxValue from a legitimate (non-saturated) sum boundary; since inputs are counts >=1 and saturation clamps at MaxValue, the 'sum < 0' test matches the original semantics. The original clamps to MaxValue once exceeded and stays there because further adds keep overflowing — identical behavior preserved. Use unchecked to avoid Burst overflow traps.
